## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sabbasaṁhārakapañhajātaka* (also attested as *Sabbasamhārakapañha*, Ja 110) is a canonical text within the Pali Jātaka collection, situated as the tenth and concluding discourse of the eleventh chapter, the *Parosatavagga* [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral].

Rather than presenting a standalone narrative at this place in the canon, the text serves as an abbreviated pointer or cross-reference. Opening with the phrase “There is no All-embracing” (*Sabbasaṁhārako natthi*), it states that this All-embracing Question will be expounded in all its aspects at length in the *Ummaggajātaka* (Ja 546) [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral]. Following this notice, the text concludes both the question itself and the *Parosatavagga* [Fausböll 1877].

In terms of parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral registers four modern translations across four languages, but lists no ancient cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus likewise finds no cross-language matches meeting the threshold score of 10 [DharmaNexus]. Within Pali literature, DharmaNexus records three matching segments totaling 306 characters shared with the first volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (the longest passage matching segments 0.4–2.2 with commentary segments 2601–2604), reflecting the commentary's reproduction and framing of the canonical passage [DharmaNexus].
